boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Scranton rituals that mark arrivals, celebrations, service, faith, and graduation.

cards.title: Make the class number
cards.subtitle: Welcome Weekend • Dionne Green
cards.notes: During Welcome Weekend, join your incoming class to form its graduation-year number for the aerial photograph; follow Student Activities directions for the current layout.
cards.short_summary: A first-year photo ritual that turns each entering class into its own year marker.
cards.evidence_claim: The University's 2026 Fall Welcome Weekend schedule calls creating the number “29” for the class aerial photo a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Fall Welcome Weekend; check the current orientation schedule for the gathering time and weather plan.

cards.title: Receive the Scranton pin
cards.subtitle: Convocation • first-year welcome
cards.notes: Attend Convocation when scheduled for your entering class; the University describes presentation of a Scranton pin there as an established beginning-of-college tradition.
cards.short_summary: The arrival counterpart to the graduation coin: a physical welcome marker.
cards.evidence_claim: University news describes presenting every student with a Scranton pin at Convocation as a well-established tradition.
cards.source_title: University of Scranton Introduces New Tradition at 2017 Commencement
cards.access_notes: Convocation timing and participation details vary by class; use the University’s current new-student communications.

cards.title: Graduate with a Coin of Excellence
cards.subtitle: Commencement • Alumni Society
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the Alumni Society’s Coin of Excellence presentation, which recognizes degree completion and welcomes graduates into the alumni community.
cards.short_summary: A commencement token linking Scranton graduates to the Alumni Society.
cards.evidence_claim: The University introduced presentation of a Coin of Excellence to graduates at commencement as a Scranton tradition in 2017.
cards.source_title: University of Scranton Introduces New Tradition at 2017 Commencement
cards.access_notes: This is tied to University commencement ceremonies; confirm ceremony instructions with the Registrar before graduation.

cards.title: Pose with the Royal family
cards.subtitle: Brennan Hall • Welcome Weekend
cards.notes: If you are the child of a Scranton alum, watch Welcome Weekend communications for the Legacy Families Reception and the photograph with the University president.
cards.short_summary: Legacy families mark both the student’s start and the transition beyond graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Legacy Families Reception and Photo has become a tradition, with incoming legacy students and families gathering with the president before Convocation.
cards.source_title: University Holds Class of 2029 Legacy Families Reception
cards.access_notes: For incoming legacy students and their families; the University announces the current year’s invitation and location.

cards.title: Open the year at the Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Byron Recreation Complex • early fall
cards.notes: Join the opening-school liturgy if it fits your practice or curiosity; Scranton follows it with a community picnic and welcomes campus participation.
cards.short_summary: A start-of-year Jesuit liturgy that brings the campus together before the academic pace settles in.
cards.evidence_claim: University news calls Scranton’s annual Mass of the Holy Spirit a long-standing tradition and reports it is held at the Byron Recreation Complex.
cards.source_title: University Celebrates Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.access_notes: Held annually near the start of the academic year; current details are announced by the University. Participation is invited, with no alcohol component.

cards.entity_name: Advent Mass and Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.title: Walk the candlelit Advent procession
cards.subtitle: Byron Center to Dionne Green • Advent
cards.notes: Attend the Advent Mass, then join the candlelit procession to Dionne Green for the blessing and lighting of the University Christmas Tree.
cards.short_summary: An Advent gathering that moves from worship to a campus tree-lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies its Advent Mass and subsequent candlelit procession to bless and light the campus Christmas Tree as a Scranton tradition.
cards.source_title: Celebrate Advent With Four Campus Traditions
cards.access_notes: Offered during Advent; the University states all are welcome. Check the current year’s event listing for time and weather arrangements.

cards.title: Hear Noel Night
cards.subtitle: Houlihan-McLean Center • holiday season
cards.notes: Reserve time for Performance Music’s annual Noel Night concert, featuring student ensembles and sacred selections alongside readings of Nativity texts.
cards.short_summary: A long-running holiday concert presented as the University’s gift to the community.
cards.evidence_claim: University news describes Noel Night as an annual holiday tradition, then in its 57th year, with student ensembles and Nativity readings.
cards.source_title: Noel Night Concert Set for Dec. 7
cards.access_notes: Held during the holiday season at the Houlihan-McLean Center; verify the current concert date and admission guidance with Performance Music.

cards.title: Bring a donation to the Empty Stocking concert
cards.subtitle: Houlihan-McLean Center • December
cards.notes: Attend the annual benefit concert with a new unwrapped toy, child’s clothing, toiletry item, or cash donation to support local families through the listed program.
cards.short_summary: A holiday performance tradition that channels admission donations into local family support.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes the Empty Stocking Fund Benefit Concert as an annual tradition and lists donation-based admission benefiting local families.
cards.source_title: Empty Stocking Fund Concert Sunday, Dec. 14
cards.access_notes: Annual December event; the 2025 listing requested a donation for admission. Confirm the current year’s accepted donation items and venue guidance.

cards.entity_name: Asian New Year Festival and Workshop
cards.title: Join the Asian New Year Festival
cards.subtitle: Asian Studies, World Cultures and Languages, and Asia Club
cards.notes: Register when the annual festival opens and take part in the presentations and hands-on activities representing Japanese, Chinese, and Taiwanese customs.
cards.short_summary: A campus cultural celebration that has returned annually since its 2011 debut.
cards.evidence_claim: The University reports that its Asian New Year festival and workshop began in 2011 and had become an annual tradition by its 14th consecutive celebration in 2024.
cards.source_title: University Welcomes Lunar New Year With Festivities, Customs
cards.access_notes: Registration was required for the documented workshop; look for the current year’s Asian Studies or student-event announcement.

cards.title: Choose an ornament from the Giving Tree
cards.subtitle: DeNaples Center, second floor • Advent
cards.notes: Choose a Giving Tree ornament, purchase an appropriate gift, and return it unwrapped to CSSJ by the announced deadline for the Gifts for Kids program.
cards.short_summary: A yearly campus giving ritual that connects a tree ornament to a child’s requested holiday gift.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls the CSSJ Christmas Giving Tree an annual initiative and instructs participants to purchase a gift for a child or teen in need.
cards.source_title: CSSJ Christmas Giving Tree Begins Nov. 13
cards.access_notes: Located in the DeNaples Center during the holiday initiative; participation requires purchasing and returning a gift by the announced deadline.
